Updated commit message as per wiki.  Let me know if anything else is needed.
Should those bytes be shown in te tree somehow? I start to wonder when bytes are skipped when looking at dissected packets and grab for the spec.

I defer to you (and others) about if these bytes should be displayed.

Just for reference, The sflow_lag spec relies on the sflow 5 spec for the definition of mac, as per sflow 5 spec these are opaque data of length 6, as per XDR spec opaque fixed length data should be 4 byte aligned (this seciton: https://tools.ietf.org/html/rfc4506#section-4.9).

`hf_sflow_lag_port_actorsystemid` and `hf_sflow_lag_port_partneropersystemid` will each have 2 bytes appended to make the total length of the opaque object a multiple of 4.

I noticed somewhat similar behavior in packet-ipdr.c with regards to skipping some bytes related to XDR:

/wireshark/epan/dissectors$ grep -B 1 -n XDR packet-ipdr.c

259-    proto_tree_add_item(samis_type_1_tree, hf_ipdr_cmts_md_if_index, tvb, offset, 4, ENC_BIG_ENDIAN);

260:    offset += 6; /* Add another 2 bytes for compatibility with XDR MAC address encoding format */

I am not implying this is what should be done, only noting that it does seem to fit with the current behavior of other dissectors.
it is better to display all bytes (and yes, there is some dissector, not yet fixed for this)
Can you point me to any protocol that I can use as a guide for how these bytes should be displayed in the tree?

Updated to show padding in a way that looked to be common in other dissectors.  Does this resolve the concern?

Example output:
```        
        LAG counters
            0000 0000 0000 0000 0000 .... .... .... = Enterprise: standard sFlow (0)
            .... .... .... .... .... 0000 0000 0111 = Format: LAG counters (7)
            Flow data length (byte): 56
            Actor System ID: Edgecore_22:26:42 (b8:6a:97:22:26:42)
            Padding: 0000
            Partner Oper System ID: ArubaaHe_25:9b:c0 (90:20:c2:25:9b:c0)
            Padding: 0000
            Port Attached Agg ID: 818
perfect !
